newsitem.title: USA: Chevron Information to cut 600 jobs.
newsitem.headline: Chevron Information to cut 600 jobs.

text.p: Chevron Corp.'s computer unit said Monday it will cut 600 jobs -- more than a third of its work force -- and add 200 employees from other Chevron units over the next two years as part of a restructuring.

Chevron Information Technology Co. also named a new president: 51-year-old Dave Clementz, now president of Chevron Petroleum Technology Co. Clementz will succeed Bill Houghton, who is retiring, on Feb. 15.

Chevron Information Technology, a wholly owned unit of the oil company, provides network computing services for Chevron's operations. It is based in San Ramon, Calif., east of San Francisco, and has about 1,600 employees.
The company expects the restructuring to save $50 million a year in costs once it is completed.
Chevron Information said 200 employees from other Chevron units providing similar services will be moved into the new organisation, consolidating personnel and equipment.
Approximately 100 positions will be eliminated in the first phase of the plan, which is expected to be completed by April 1.
In 1998, about 500 additional positions will be eliminated as operations are streamlined, contracted out or discontinued, the company said.
By the end of 1998, Chevron Information expects to have about 1,200 employees.
